title: Chapter 77 — Emotional Intelligence and Self-Regulation
intro: Self-awareness, regulation under pressure, empathy that serves, and managing the emotional labour of selling.

sections.title: Self-Awareness on the Floor
sections.content:
Before you can read a customer's emotions, you need to manage your own. A bad morning, a lost sale, a difficult customer — all of these affect your energy. And customers feel your energy before they hear your words.

The salesperson who walks up frustrated from the last interaction carries that into the next greeting. The customer senses it immediately — even if they cannot name it.

Between customers, reset. Take a breath. Let go of the last interaction. Every customer deserves a fresh version of you.

sections.title: Regulation Under Pressure
sections.content:
Customers sometimes get frustrated, demanding, or unreasonable. The professional response is always the same: stay calm, stay helpful, and do not take it personally.

This is harder than it sounds. But it is a skill, not a personality trait. It can be practiced and developed. The salesperson who can stay composed when a customer is venting about a competitor's broken delivery promise earns enormous trust. Calm is contagious.

sections.title: Empathy That Serves
sections.content:
Empathy in sales does not mean feeling what the customer feels. It means understanding what they feel and using that understanding to help them.

A customer who is stressed about a broken refrigerator does not need sympathy. They need someone who understands the urgency and solves the problem quickly. A customer who is overwhelmed by options does not need more options. They need someone who narrows the field with confidence.

Empathy is a diagnostic tool. It tells you what the customer needs from you right now.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating emotional intelligence, ask:

Does the salesperson reset between customers — or carry baggage?
Do they stay composed under pressure — or mirror the customer's frustration?
Do they use empathy to understand and serve — or to bond without purpose?
Is their emotional energy consistent throughout the day — or does it decline?
